The player must first locate blue_carpet (which serves as a visual trail/guide on the floor), then find black_stained_glass_pane (windows in a room), then find purple_wool (decorative block near the bedroom), and finally mine blue_bed (which is in the bedroom). The dependency chain reflects a logical spatial exploration: the carpet leads to the windowed room, the glass panes indicate the correct wing of the building, the purple_wool marks the bedroom entrance, and the blue_bed is the final target to mine inside that bedroom. This creates a natural navigation puzzle without requiring deep Minecraft crafting knowledge.

scene_description: A two-room oak plank house on a stone brick foundation. The player spawns outside and follows a blue carpet trail through the front door into the main hall. The main hall has black stained glass pane windows on both side walls. A dividing wall separates the main hall from the bedroom, with purple wool blocks framing the bedroom doorway. Inside the bedroom is a blue bed that must be mined.

Interior dividing wall at x=6 separates main hall (z=6-10) from bedroom (z=11-17). Purple wool frames the bedroom doorway at ~6,0/2,12 and ~6,0/2,14. Blue bed is at ~9-10,0,14 in the bedroom. Torches provide lighting.
